title: The conductivity matrix at the topological phase transition
authors: Simone Fabbri, Giovanna Marcelli, Alessandro Giuliani
abstract: For a general class of two-dimensional non-interacting semi-metallic electron systems on a lattice, we derive an explicit formula for the whole conductivity matrix, by using Euclidean many-body formalism. The semi-metallic phase takes place whenever two Bloch bands touch at the Fermi energy with conical intersections and generally occurs at the transition between distinct integer quantum Hall phases. Unlike the longitudinal conductivity (which depends solely on the shape of the cones at the Fermi level), the transverse conductivity is remarkably determined both by the conical structures of the bands and by the nature of the two nearby topological phases. Generically, in the semi-metallic state, neither the longitudinal nor the transverse conductivities are quantized in integer multiples of a universal conductivity quantum; however, universality of the conductivity matrix is restored under the assumption of emergent rotational symmetry of the linearized Hamiltonian at the Fermi points. Using our formula, we compute the conductivity matrix for several physically relevant models of quantum Hall fluids at the topological phase transition, exhibiting cases where the transverse conductivity is quantized in half-integer multiples of $e^2/h$ and cases where it depends continuously on an external strain parameter, thus shedding light on its universality or non-universality features.
summary: This theoretical work derives the conductivity matrix for 2D semi-metallic electron systems undergoing a topological phase transition. While the general prediction is non-quantized conductivity, the authors show that imposing an emergent rotational symmetry restores quantization, particularly for the anti-symmetric part of the matrix. This sheds light on the conditions under which transport properties become robust topological invariants.
main_problem: The paper aims to derive an explicit formula for the entire conductivity matrix at a topological phase transition (TPT) in 2D non-interacting semi-metallic electron systems.
main_result: Generally, the conductivity matrix is not quantized, but universality is restored under the assumption of emergent rotational symmetry, leading to quantized values for the anti-symmetric part of the matrix.
method: The analysis uses the Euclidean many-body formalism and the Kubo formula, calculating the critical conductivity by averaging results from both sides of the transition.
model_or_system: The system is a general class of 2D non-interacting electron systems on a lattice, modeled by a Hamiltonian that exhibits semi-metallic behavior when two Bloch bands touch at conical intersections.
key_observables: The full conductivity matrix $\sigma$, specifically the longitudinal ($\sigma_{ii}$) and transverse ($\sigma_{12}$) conductivities.
important_parameters: The mass parameter $m$ controlling the TPT, the Fermi energy, and the external strain parameter.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system is non-interacting and disorder-free, and for quantization results, it crucially assumes the existence of emergent discrete rotational invariance.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing the general formula for $\sigma(m)$ using the Euclidean formalism, then analyzing the limits at the TPT ($m=0$), and finally discussing specific physical models and the conditions required for quantization.
why_interesting: The rigorous derivation of transport coefficients like the conductivity matrix at a critical point, especially linking it to topological invariants under specific symmetry assumptions, is highly relevant to understanding quantum transport in novel materials.
